text:
alan: Heads up — multiple customers reporting hourly usage charts dropped to 0 after the 09:02 deploy. Not seeing errors in UI, just missing rows in the hourly_rollups table.
ops-bot: alert: hourly_ingest_lag > 1h for group=hourly-ingest (10 tenants).
riley: I'll grab consumer group status. Can someone share the deploy hash?
alan: deploy: d9f3a7b (service-common bumped).
maya: checking logs now. Quick grep shows consumer restarted at 09:03 and then OOMs a few times.
riley: kafka-consumer-groups output: ```
GROUP           TOPIC           PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG
hourly-ingest   usage_events    12         54231           999999          945768
hourly-ingest   usage_events    13         54200           54205           5
```
lee: partition 12 lag looks brutal — likely consumer process crashed and didn't resume. I see repeated GC pauses in the pod logs: ```java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space```
jordan: That partition houses the high-throughput tenants. If we restart the consumer it will start processing but might thrash. Suggest draining partition to a fresh consumer with larger heap then backfill small gaps.
support-bot: Customer impact: dashboards showing zeros for hours 09:00-11:00 for affected tenants. Several tickets opened (see #support-tickets/3412).
alan: Can we run a targeted backfill for the stuck window instead of full reprocessing?
riley: Yes — run the backfill for partitions 12 only with start offset 54232 to 999999. Command I plan to run: ```bash
./tools/backfill.py --topic usage_events --partition 12 --from-offset 54232 --to-offset 999999 --target-table hourly_rollups --batch-size 1000
```
maya: Before that, I'll spin a replacement consumer with heap=6g and attach the lagging partition to it. That should drain faster and avoid reprocessing too many duplicates.
alan: ETA for consumer up?
maya: +10m. After that we'll let it drain for ~20–30m, then backfill remaining offsets if needed.
sam: I'll notify affected customers with a short note: we're aware, root cause is consumer OOM after recent common lib update, working on restart and backfill.
jordan: Also checking S3 commit logs — saw a couple of tombstones around 09:01 that might have caused aggregator to skip keys. Will include tombstone handling in backfill script.
lee: Quick mitigation for dashboards: change the hourly chart to fall back to 24h-aggregates when hourly rows are missing. I can patch the frontend route for a temporary toggle.
alan: Good — do that. Support, please add one-sentence status to each open ticket.
support-bot: Updated tickets with current mitigations and ETA 2h.
riley: Killed the crashed pod and started new consumer with bigger heap. Lag is moving: partition 12 lag dropped from 945k to 200k in 12m.
maya: Starting the targeted backfill now for remaining range (script above). Posting logs to S3: s3://redwood-ops/backfill/1813456789-run.log
sam: I'll monitor errors and customer replies. If anything changes, ping @on-call.
alan: Thanks all — will follow up after backfill completes and when dashboards show recovered numbers. :thumbsup:
